build.note: Offline modelling on the 14 and 15 October captures (L4040 to L4043) and read-only decoding of 2.1.1.0 GS assets; no new capture, game not launched.

question: Does a structural change to the recovery law (two-term recovery, a cap on recovery rate, a cap on the time term) reproduce the three 15 October symptoms (the 290 to 350 ms tail, the missing Lightened advantage in the LMR27 tail, the 15-round TR-7 excess)? Where in a 15-round TR-7 burst do game and model diverge? Do the unread recoil fields separate the steep-profile weapons from the AK-205?

sourceFacts.method: variant-sim2.mjs (copy of the 14 October integrator with twoRate, twoPool, rateCap and timeCap variants; identical to variant-sim.mjs on the base variants) fitted with fit-shape.mjs (same 46 observations, 500 seeds and scoring as fit-tail3.mjs; the TR-7 200 ms Standard band is now actually excluded, see ANALYSIS.md). Per-shot climb from a re-detection of the stars in the six 15-round close-up screenshots with the bursts1x.py detector. Fields from frosty-ebx-decode.py on the 2.1.1.0 GS assets (the Z84M from the season-5 uncaptured-routes report) cross-checked against the 1.4.3.0 raw audit.

control.description: variant-sim2 equals variant-sim to 0 on 3 weapons x 3 base settings x 2 seeds x 15 shots; the re-detected panel boxes equal bursts1x.json; every 2.1.1.0 field value read equals the 1.4.3.0 raw audit value for the eight weapons both cover.

points: Fits over 45 usable observations: applied x0.8 476.7, best of the 15 October family 432.5; two-rate (rate sum, no offset) 446.4 at best; two-pool (10% of each kick into a slow pool at 2/s) 410.4; time cap 0.2 s 420.5; recovery-rate cap 8 deg/s with x0.8 and offset 0.03 347.5 (bursts 97.6 against 182.6); best combination timeCap Tcap=0.2 C=0.8 offset=0.06 + Rmax=8 329.8.

No variant reproduces all three symptoms. The 290 to 350 ms tail (observed 0.105 deg mean over three bands) is at most 0.1 deg in any variant under chi2 500; the LMR27 Lightened band at 340 to 350 ms stays below the Standard in every variant (best 0.163 against 0.225, observed 0.185 and 0.189); the rate cap lifts the 15-round TR-7 Standard from 8.673 to 9.522 deg (observed 11.19) but pushes the 10-round from 6.474 to 6.662 (observed 6.02).

Per-shot climb: the six 15-round close-ups resolve 7 to 14 marks per spray (none all 15). The fraction of marks in the lower half of a spray is 0.591 (Standard, 4 sprays) and 0.674 (Lightened, 7) against 0.406 / 0.391 for the x0.8 law with spread, 0.45 for the rate cap and 0.53 for a linear climb: the game climbs less than the law over the first half of the burst and more over the second; the law is concave where the game is convex.

Unread fields (2.1.1.0, ADS): VerticalRecoilIncrease 0 on all nine except the LMR27 (0.6); VerticalRecoilMin/Max 0.578/0.578 on all six steep-profile weapons, 0.42/0.42 AK-205, 0.6/0 LMR27, 0/0 M433; MaxVerticalRecoil 20; FirstShotMultiplierVerticalRecoil 1; RecoilPatternMultiplierPitch/Yaw 0 and seed 0; HorizontalRecoilLeft/Right 0.3/-0.6 on the steep profile, 0.2/-0.3 AK-205 and M433, 0.2/-0.2 LMR27; CameraRecoil springs 1500/1500, damping 0.94/0.5, exponent 30/50, UseTimeSinceLastShot true on all nine. The Smooth modifier (GRM_SmoothRecoil_P10) carries RecoilDecreaseFactor x1.2 and RecoilDuration override 0.05 in both aim states and nothing else.

inference: The misfit is not in the shape of the recovery term alone: no single- or two-term recovery, rate cap or time cap reproduces the tail, the Lightened tail and the TR-7 late climb together, and the burst evidence now says the game's climb accelerates through a 15-round burst, which no recovery-only law can produce (recovery can only slow the climb as recoil accumulates). The missing piece acts on the kick or on recovery as a function of accumulated recoil, and the unread GS fields offer no per-weapon operand that would single out the steep profile: the only values that differ are VerticalRecoilMin/Max (0.578 against 0.42) and the horizontal bounds.
unresolved: Per-shot impact positions from the burst videos (the close-ups merge early marks); whether VerticalRecoilMin/Max or MaxVerticalRecoil enter the live climb; the native composition of the Smooth multiply with a tail.
siteImpact: None applied; the x0.8 scale stands. A recovery-rate cap near 8 deg/s would improve the 15-round TR-7 fit but worsen the 10-round one and has no mechanism; not proposed.

leads.title: Recovery-law shape study: no two-term, rate-capped or time-capped recovery reproduces the tail, the Lightened tail and the TR-7 late climb together; the 15-round TR-7 climb is convex where every recovery law is concave; the unread recoil fields do not single out the steep profile
leads.summary: Over the 14 and 15 October observations the applied x0.8 law scores 476.7, the best offset variant 432.5, a two-pool recovery 410.4, a time cap 420.5, a recovery-rate cap of 8 deg/s 347.5 and the best combination 329.8; none matches the 290 to 350 ms tail, the equal Lightened and Standard LMR27 bands at 340 to 350 ms, or the 15-round TR-7 extent without over-predicting the 10-round one. The 15-round TR-7 close-ups put 0.591 to 0.674 of the marks in the lower half of the spray against 0.39 to 0.41 for the law: the climb accelerates through the burst. The nine weapons' unread fields (2.1.1.0) differ only in VerticalRecoilMin/Max and the horizontal bounds; the Smooth modifier is x1.2 on the factor and 0.05 s duration, nothing more.
leads.reopenWhen: Per-shot impact positions from the burst videos, or a capture on the 72 / 1.2 profile with 10, 15 and 20-round bursts, or a readable implementation of the recoil kick and recovery.
